input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

team.claim: Nik Storonsky and Vlad Yatsenko co-founded Revolut. The FY2025 report identifies Storonsky as CEO, Victor Stinga as CFO and Martin Gilbert as chairman; this is the latest opened annual-report leadership baseline, signed in March 2026, not a complete current statutory-officer check.

Founder backgrounds: Storonsky previously worked at Lehman Brothers and Credit Suisse; Yatsenko built financial software at UBS, Deutsche Bank and Credit Suisse, following software roles at Comarch and Sabre Airline Solutions.

Reuters reported that Yatsenko would leave the CTO position and become a non-executive director on 2026-07-01. Donato Lucia, then head of technology, would replace him as Vice President of Technology; calling Lucia CTO would overstate the title reported.

funding.claim: Company-reported historical primary rounds: Series A, $15 million in 2016; Series B, $66 million in 2017; Series C, $250 million in 2018; Series D, $580 million in 2020. Amounts and years are the annual report’s historical milestones; exact closing dates and lead investors are not specified there.
Company announcement: $800 million Series E from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Tiger Global, at a $33 billion valuation as of 2021-07-15.

Company announcement: completed share sale at a $75 billion valuation as of 2025-11-24, led by Coatue, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Fidelity Management & Research; participants included a16z, Franklin Templeton, T. Rowe Price-advised accounts and NVentures. Employees could sell; do not treat this liquidity event as an $75 billion primary capital raise. Transaction proceeds were not disclosed on the opened announcement.

Latest reported valuation: Reuters described Revolut as valued at $115 billion as of 2026-10-04. Its 2026-07-22 report said a secondary sale was underway and attributed that valuation to a person familiar with the sale; the company confirmed the process, not its pricing. Completion, proceeds and latest investor allocation remain unverified.

output.verdict: As of 2026-11-03, Revolut merits further diligence: reported profitable growth, a diversified fee-led model and UK bank launch are strengths. Before underwriting the reported $115 billion valuation, prioritise AML remediation, Italian consumer-protection findings, fraud reimbursement and the September data-disclosure incident, alongside confirmation of secondary-sale terms and leadership continuity.

business.claim: Scope: Revolut group, headed by Revolut Group Holdings Ltd; regulated banking and investment services are delivered through separate subsidiaries, not by a single universally licensed entity.

Company description: consumer app for spending, transfers, foreign exchange, saving, investing and borrowing; Revolut Business supplies payments, expense and cash-flow management, treasury and merchant-acceptance services.
Company claim: served customers across 39 countries and operated as a licensed bank in 30 countries as of 2025-12-31; products and permissions differ by jurisdiction.

Company-reported monetisation: fees were 76% of FY2025 turnover; interest income was 21.6%. Card payments contributed 22.2%, subscriptions 15.7%, wealth 14.7% and foreign exchange 13.4% for the year ended 2025-12-31.

traction.claim: Company claim: retail customers reached 68.3 million at 2025-12-31, up 30% year on year; business customers reached 767,000, up 33%. These are customer counts, not disclosed active-user counts.

Company claim: total customer balances reached £50.2 billion at 2025-12-31, up 66% year on year. This measure includes deposits, savings with partners and Flexible Cash Funds; it is not solely bank deposits.

Company claim: Revolut Business accounted for 16% of FY2025 group revenue and processed £277 billion of transaction volume during the year ended 2025-12-31; Booking.com and Vueling were named travel-sector partners.
Company claim: payment-acceptance volume rose 228% year on year and Revolut Pay was used by 4.8 million users during FY2025, ended 2025-12-31.

red_flags.claim: Control-scaling risk: the Lithuanian banking subsidiary’s €3.5 million AML/CTF fine warrants testing remediation and independent control assurance before investment.

Consumer-conduct risk: Italy’s €11.5 million fines cover investment disclosures, account restrictions and IBAN communications; verify remediation and the appeal outcome rather than assuming the matter is resolved.

Information-security risk: September 2026 disclosure of sensitive customer information through fraudulent official-domain requests warrants review of government-request authentication and incident controls.

Customer-remediation risk: the fraud-complaint volumes and partial uphold rate reported by Which? warrant testing reimbursement decisions, complaint handling and operational capacity; the data do not establish a per-customer fraud incidence rate.
Valuation/execution risk: the reported $115 billion private valuation raises underwriting sensitivity to future growth and monetisation; latest sale completion and investment terms remain unverified.

reputation.claim: Which?, using Financial Ombudsman Service FOI data, reported 3,242 Revolut authorised-push-payment fraud complaints referred in calendar 2024. For 2025-01-01 through 2025-08-31, it reported 1,875 APP cases and a 30% uphold rate. Counts are not customer-normalised fraud rates, and decisions may concern older incidents.

Aggregator evidence: Glassdoor displayed 4.3/5 from 6,583 reviews and 84% recommending Revolut, observed as of 2026-11-03. These are self-selected employee reviews, not a representative workforce survey; a reliable historical overall-rating trend was not established.

Reuters’ 2026-10-04 analysis highlighted lower revenue per customer than established banks and a comparatively small lending business. These are critical press assessments, not evidence of insolvency or misconduct.

financial_signals.claim: Company-reported FY2025 revenue was £4.5 billion, up 46% year on year, and profit before tax was £1.7 billion, up 57%, for the year ended 2025-12-31. These are reported results, not third-party estimates.

Annual-report employee disclosure: year-end group headcount rose from 10,133 at 2024-12-31 to 12,200 at 2025-12-31; average monthly employees were 9,932 in FY2024 and 10,909 in FY2025. Year-end and annual-average measures should not be mixed.
Company claim as of 2026-03-11: committed to invest £3 billion and create 1,000 high-skilled UK jobs. This is a forward-looking commitment, not confirmed expenditure or completed hiring.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Company announcement: PRA lifted mobilisation restrictions and approved launch of Revolut Bank UK Ltd on 2026-03-11. Customer migration was to be phased; existing e-money accounts did not all immediately become bank accounts or receive deposit protection.

Bank of Lithuania records a €3.5 million fine against Revolut Bank UAB dated 2025-04-04 for AML/CTF-law and supervisory-instruction breaches. This is a subsidiary enforcement action, not evidence of a sanctions violation by the parent.

Italy’s AGCM announced €11.5 million in fines on 2026-04-02: €5 million concerning investment disclosures against Revolut Securities Europe UAB and Revolut Group Holdings Ltd; €5 million concerning account restrictions and €1.5 million concerning Italian IBAN disclosures against Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and Revolut Bank UAB. These are authority findings, not merely an open investigation.
Reuters reported that Revolut strongly disagreed with the Italian authority and intended to appeal. An intention to appeal is not proof that an appeal was filed or that the findings were overturned.

In [2026] EWHC 64 (Admin), Revolut Bank UAB participated with Visa and Mastercard in challenging the Payment Systems Regulator’s power to cap cross-border interchange fees; the claims were dismissed on 2026-01-15. This was litigation brought by the banking subsidiary, not a damages judgment against the parent.

Reuters reported Revolut’s confirmation that sensitive customer information was disclosed to an unauthorised party following fraudulent requests from a legitimate government-agency email domain. As of 2026-09-12, Revolut said affected customers had been notified and systems and customer funds were unaffected; it did not disclose an exact affected-customer count.

Company sanctions policy says it screens customers and applicable transactions against UN, EU, UK, US and relevant local lists and blocks or rejects prohibited activity. This is a statement of policy, not independent evidence of effective controls or a clean enforcement history; assessed as of 2026-11-03.
